blockers:
claim: Race condition on m_channelCount: written in applyConnectedState() and read in pollChannelSupport() without synchronization; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: m_channelCount = std::min<uint32_t>(info.channel_count,
                                            ECUIO_SESSION_INFO_MAX_CHANNELS);
claim: Race condition on m_supportGeneration array: written in pollChannelSupport() without mutex or atomic protection; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: m_supportGeneration[c] = s.generation;
questions: Is pollChannelSupport() called from the same thread as pollLinkHealth()? If not, the unsynchronized access to m_supportGeneration is a data race.
What is the threading model for m_session? Can it be concurrently modified or set to nullptr while pollChannelSupport() is executing?
Should m_channelCount and m_supportGeneration be std::atomic or protected by a mutex given they are accessed from multiple threads?
nits: The ranges loop only checks bits 0-7 but should verify if ranges field can have higher bits set that would indicate PIDs beyond the 0xFF limit being checked.
Consider using std::atomic<uint32_t> for m_channelCount to ensure visibility across threads.
The non-atomic read of m_session could be made safer with an atomic store/load pattern matching the m_connected approach.
